meta.title: Markdown to PDF
meta.description: Adds an export-to-PDF action for Markdown in the right sidebar's file tabs: open a .md file as a tab and the tab header shows a PDF button, the path label offers the same row on right-click, and a .md row in the workspace tree can be exported the same way. The PDF is written next to the source file with the same base name. Markdown rendered in the conversation is not covered. Rendering keeps headings, tables, task lists, footnotes, code blocks, images, frontmatter and TeX math, and embeds a CJK font so Chinese and Japanese text prints correctly. Lists follow GitHub-flavored Markdown, so a list may start on the line right after a paragraph without a blank line between them. No pandoc, LaTeX or other command-line tool is required: math becomes MathML inside the plugin and the browser lays it out. The dsh-md2pdf page in Settings treats layout presets as editable templates: Lark (the default), an official document preset built on GB/T 9704-2012, and an academic paper preset built on GB/T 7713.2-2022; the two national-standard presets use three-line tables. Click a card to use a preset, click the blue bar under it to edit that preset's CSS, and create, reorder or delete presets from the same page. Saving asks for a name and confirms before replacing an existing one. An Open button beside the stylesheet path edits that preset's CSS in your own editor. Every preset shows a thumbnail of a really rendered page, and below the editor a larger preview shows the preset in use; an unmodified national-standard preset carries a badge. A preset change applies to the next export. Printing uses the system's Chromium engine, such as Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome; when the host process can load Electron, it prints from the application's own process instead. No file content leaves the machine, and nothing is uploaded. Turning the plugin off removes every control, the settings page and the md2pdf_export tool.
